summary: formatJsonReadable (web/src/lib/format.js) JSON.stringifies any object and hard-caps at 120 chars. The only structured-object consumer was StatusBanner's publish-lint violations list (screen-process-editor.jsx) — server LintViolation objects ({type, elementId, elementKind, message}, src/core/bpmn-linter.ts). The {type,elementId,elementKind} JSON envelope alone eats ~105-110 of the 120 chars, so a long .message (e.g. timer_escalation_no_convergence, whose 550+-char message carries a 'Fix: ...' hint at the tail — docs/design/ADR-T0612-purchase-escalation-convergence.md) survived truncation as ~12 unreadable characters. Systemic across every LintViolationType with a long message, not just timer-convergence — confirmed by reading src/core/bpmn-linter.ts (11 violation types, several with multi-clause messages) and the two actual formatJsonReadable call sites (grep confirmed only screen-process-editor.jsx's violations list and screen-record-detail.jsx's unrelated generic field-value fallback).
fix: Client-render-only, server contract untouched (violations shape/422 envelope unchanged). screen-process-editor.jsx: new VIOLATION_TYPE_LABELS (Russian rule title per LintViolationType, all 11 current types covered; unmapped/future type falls back to the raw .type string — additive, never blocks render) + new ViolationItem({v}) component: string violations render as-is (role-warning back-compat); object violations with a string .message render a structured entry (rule title + 'elementKind «elementId»' context + the FULL .message, never truncated, CSS white-space:pre-wrap so it wraps instead of clipping); anything else falls back to the prior formatJsonReadable(v) behaviour (dead code path today — the linter never emits a violation without .message — kept as a safety net, not a regression). StatusBanner's violations list now maps to <ViolationItem/> instead of calling formatJsonReadable(v) directly. editor.css: .chs-banner__violation{,-title,-element,-message} rules (spacing + wrap), no hardcoded colors (design tokens only). format.js: formatJsonReadable's implementation and 120-char behaviour are UNCHANGED — only a doc-comment records the new invariant ('don't use this for structured errors') for future readers; its existing generic-preview consumer (screen-record-detail.jsx field fallback) is untouched and re-verified (its 43+3 tests still pass).
deviations_from_adr: No ADR existed for this task (T-0659 is a render-bug fix, not an architectural decision) — spec.md documents the fix layer and AC instead.

Left the formatJsonReadable(v) fallback branch in ViolationItem for object violations without a .message, even though src/core/bpmn-linter.ts's LintViolation always carries .message today — defensive, not required by the task; documented in spec.md as 'не в скоупе' / AC4.

tests_added.covers: 5 new node-env tests (project convention: call the component as a function, tree-walk the returned tree — no DOM) against the exported, hook-free ViolationItem: (1) a 550+-char timer_escalation_no_convergence-shaped message renders in FULL including the trailing 'Fix: ...' hint, with no '…' ellipsis anywhere in the output — RED before this fix (the old formatJsonReadable(v) call would have cut it to 120 chars + '…'); (2) .type translates to the Russian rule title + shows elementKind/elementId context; (3) an unmapped/future .type falls back to the raw type string without crashing; (4) plain-string violations (role-warning shape) still render as-is; (5) an object violation with no .message falls back to formatJsonReadable. StatusBanner itself (has a useEffect) is NOT tree-walked directly — it needs a real React runtime, covered by the mount test below instead.

NEW file — REAL DOM mount via @testing-library/react + jsdom (@vitest-environment jsdom), scoped to the exported StatusBanner (not the full ProcessEditorScreen, which embeds the real bpmn-js canvas — out of scope for a violation-rendering fix). 4 tests: mounts with a long lint violation and asserts screen.getByText finds the FULL message + the Russian rule title + the 'Fix:' hint in the real DOM; mounts a mixed violations array (string + structured object + unknown no-message shape) without throwing; renders null without crashing when there is no active message; renders without crashing when isError=true but violations=[] (empty array edge case). Catches real-DOM crashes the node-env tree-walk convention structurally cannot see (D-064 rationale — see FormDesigner.mount.test.jsx).
